findings.reason: the output-preservation mechanism §12 introduces (recording each file the scan drops so the invalid-resource-path findings survive the move to iter_resources) is exactly the thing at risk when the walk changes, and the declared control cannot show it fires, so the gate would pass a node that changed the audit's findings; the author should add a control that drops collided files without recording them and require the equal-findings case to fail, as §13 now does for its own parse half.
findings.text: §12's done-when asserts both "the tree is walked once" and "The audit's findings for that corpus are equal to its findings before the change", but its sole declared negative control ("restores the audit's own rglob walk, and the walk-count case must then fail") only falsifies the walk-count half: restoring the rglob leaves the audit emitting its invalid-resource-path findings from its own loop, so the findings stay equal and that assertion is never shown to be able to fail
